card: This pull request exposes the internal block announcement timestamp as last_block_announcement in the getpeerinfo RPC result. Previously, this timestamp was only accessible internally for stale-tip eviction logic, making it impossible for node operators to evaluate peer announcement responsiveness and preventing functional test verification of the announcement tracking logic fixed in #26172. The change also modernizes the internal timestamp representation to NodeClock::time_point and adds a functional test verifying that timestamps update only on novel headers with superior chainwork.
evidence: "The functional test added here fails without #26172, which is the main goal." (PR description)
"This PR started out as a suggestion for additional test coverage, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/26172#issuecomment-1259678260." (PR description)
problem: Node operators cannot inspect when a peer was the first to announce a new block, nor predict which outbound peer would be evicted when stale tip detection triggers. Additionally, because this internal timestamp was not observable via RPC, functional tests could not directly verify peer announcement tracking or prevent regressions like the one fixed in #26172.
scope_notes: Changes the internal type of CNodeState::m_last_block_announcement from int64_t to NodeClock::time_point, passes it through CNodeStateStats into rpc/net.cpp, and introduces the functional test p2p_block_times.py.
summary: Exposes the internal peer timestamp tracking the latest block announcement as `last_block_announcement` in the `getpeerinfo` RPC result. It also updates the internal timestamp type to `NodeClock::time_point` and adds a functional test verifying announcement timestamp behavior.
